name: lysine methyltransferase 2C
pathways: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

function.text: KMT2C encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase 2C. Annotated molecular activities include histone methyltransferase activity and transcription coactivator activity. It participates in positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to syndromic intellectual disability (autosomal dominant); Kleefstra syndrome 2 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic sequence alterations have cohort-level candidate-driver evidence in Invasive Breast Carcinoma; Prostate Adenocarcinoma; Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma. This gene-level statistical evidence requires allele-specific review and does not establish the effect of every variant.

function.text: KMT2C encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase 2C. It is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4). It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery predominantly forms H3K4me1 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It likely plays a redundant role with KMT2D in enriching H3K4me1 mark on primed and active enhancer elements.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with syndromic intellectual disability (autosomal dominant); Kleefstra syndrome 2 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving KMT2C have been reported in melanoma, pancreas, and prostate.
